'''Eric Mika''' (born January 5, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]].

==High school career==
Mika played at [[Waterford School]] his freshman and sophomore seasons before attending [[Lone Peak High School]] in [[Highland, Utah]] for his final 2 seasons. Mika help lead Lone Peak to a 26–1 record, the 2012-13 MaxPreps.com National Title and the 5A Utah state title with other future BYU Cougars Nick Emery and T.J. Haws.

==College career==
Mika played college basketball for [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Nathan Cunningham |title=BYU basketball: Eric Mika named Center of the Year Award finalist |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-basketball/byu-basketball-eric-mika-named-center-of-the-year-award-finalist |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[Fox Sports]] |date=30 June 2017}}</ref> He was named to the WCC All-Freshman Team and averaged double figures in points.

Mika returned to a BYU team and in his first season back from the mission field in [[2016–17 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|2016–17]] he averaged 20.3 points and 9.2 rebounds a game. Mika was named to the All-[[West Coast Conference]] team.

==Professional career==
===Consultinvest Pesaro (2017–2018)===
Mika declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] after his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite news|title=BYU leading scorer Eric Mika to remain in NBA draft, hire agent |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19404810/byu-cougars-forward-eric-mika-remain-nba-draft-hire-agent|accessdate=July 20, 2017|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=May 17, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Jay Drew |title=BYU basketball: Eric Mika will remain in NBA Draft |url=https://archive.sltrib.com/article.php?id=5299039&itype=CMSID |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |date=16 May 2017}}</ref> After going undrafted,<ref>{{cite news |author1=Charles Rex Arbogast |title=Inside Darnell's Head: Mika goes deep on why he left BYU |url=https://www.heraldextra.com/sports/2018/aug/06/inside-darnells-head-mika-goes-deep-on-why-he-left-byu/ |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[Daily Herald (Utah)|Daily Herald]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=6 August 2018}}</ref> Mika joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[NBA Summer League]], then ultimately signed with [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Consultinvest Pesaro]] in Italy.<ref>{{cite news|title=Eric Mika nuovo centro della VL|url=http://www.victorialibertas.it/index.php/news/news-17-18/588-eric-mika-nuovo-centro-della-vl|accessdate=July 20, 2017|work=[[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Consultinvest Pesaro]]|date=July 20, 2017|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171114160758/http://www.victorialibertas.it/index.php/news/news-17-18/588-eric-mika-nuovo-centro-della-vl|archive-date=November 14, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Basket Brescia Leonessa (2018–2019)===
On July 9, 2018, Mika signed a deal with [[Basket Brescia Leonessa]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Leonessa Brescia signs Eric Mika|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/281007/leonessa-brescia-signs-eric-mika.html|accessdate=July 10, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=July 9, 2018|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206163354/https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/281007/leonessa-brescia-signs-eric-mika.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Medi Bayreuth (2019)===
On January 8, 2019, Mika signed a contract with [[Medi Bayreuth]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/806727/bayreuth-signs-eric-mika/|title=Bayreuth signs Eric Mika|date=January 8, 2019|publisher=Eurohoops|language=en|access-date=April 17, 2019}}</ref>

===Stockton Kings (2019)===
On August 20, 2019, Mika signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Mitch Harper |title=Years After Leaving BYU, Eric Mika Gets His NBA Opportunity |url=https://kslsports.com/415021/eric-mika-sacramento-kings-nba-opportunity/ |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=KSL Sports |date=20 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Eric Mika|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-eric-mika|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 27, 2019|date=August 20, 2019}}</ref> On October 11, 2019, Mika was waived by the Kings<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings Waive Eric Mika and Isaiah Pineiro |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-waive-eric-mika-and-isaiah-pineiro |website=NBA.com |accessdate=October 16, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> and ultimately included in the roster of [[Stockton Kings]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2019-20 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2019-20-training-camp-roster|date=October 28, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 28, 2019|archive-date=January 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112213530/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2019-20-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[NBA G League]] affiliate team of the [[Sacramento Kings]].

===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2019)===
On December 6, 2019, the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] announced that they had added Mika to their roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=同意新疆伊力特队更换外籍球员官方公告|language=ZH|url=https://www.cbaleague.com/#/news/announcement/detail/109|date=December 6, 2019|website=cbaleague.com|accessdate=December 6, 2019}}</ref> On December 27, 2019, Mika was removed from the roster of the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=同意新疆伊力特队更换外籍球员官方公告|language=ZH|url=https://www.cbaleague.com/#/news/announcement/detail/146|date=December 27, 2019|website=cbaleague.com|accessdate=December 27, 2019}}</ref>

===Second stint with Stockton Kings (2020)===
On January 7, 2020, the [[Stockton Kings]] announced that they had acquired Mika.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings acquire forward Eric Mika|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-acquire-forward-eric-mika|date=January 7, 2020|website=NBA.com|accessdate=January 7, 2020|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030194019/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-acquire-forward-eric-mika/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Sean Walker |title=Thousands of miles later, former BYU star Eric Mika's road to NBA as close as it's ever been |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46709097/thousands-of-miles-later-former-byu-star-eric-mikas-road-to-nba-as-close-as-its-ever-been |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[KSL.com]] |date=25 January 2020}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2020)===
On February 1, 2020, Mika signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Ryan McDonald |title=Former Lone Peak, BYU Cougars standout Eric Mika signs with NBA's Sacramento Kings |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/2/1/21118607/former-lone-peak-byu-cougars-standout-eric-mika-signs-with-nbas-sacramento-kings |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[Deseret News]] |date=1 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Kings Sign Eric Mika to 10-Day Contract|url= https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-eric-mika-10-day-contract|date=February 1, 2020|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 1, 2020}}</ref> He made his NBA debut the same day, scoring six points with seven rebounds in 19 minutes as the Kings lost to the [[2019–20 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]] 129–113. On February 6, the [[Sacramento Kings]] announced that they had requested waiver on Mika.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Acquire Alex Len and Jabari Parker Team Sends Dewayne Dedmon, Two Future Second-Round Picks to Atlanta. Team Requests Waivers on Eric Mika.|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-alex-len-and-jabari-parker|date=February 6, 2020|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Third stint with Stockton Kings (2020)===
Mika was reported to have returned to [[Stockton Kings]] after being waived by the [[Sacramento Kings]] on February 6, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eric Mika: Dominates in return to G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/eric-mika-dominates-in-return-to-g-league|date=February 11, 2020|website=cbssports.com|accessdate=February 11, 2020}}</ref> He averaged  18.7 points and 11.9 rebounds per game in the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Partizan NIS, Eric Mika agree to deal |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/partizan-nis-eric-mika-agree-to-deal/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=August 24, 2020 |date=August 24, 2020|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>

===Partizan Belgrade (2020–2021)===
On August 24, 2020, Mika signed a contract with the [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=Mitch Harper |title=Former BYU Great Eric Mika Signs With Partizan BC In Serbia |url=https://kslsports.com/440499/eric-mika-partizan-signs/ |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=KSL Sports |date=24 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Erik Mika je novo pojačanje Partizana|url=http://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/2814/erik-mika-je-novo-pojacanje-partizana|date=August 24, 2020|newspaper=Normacore.com|accessdate=August 24, 2020 |last1=Normasoft. Net |first1=Normasoft }}</ref> He averaged 7.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game.<ref name=yahyabeyoglu>{{cite web |last1=Gajic |first1=Andrija |title=Eric Mika, Basketball Player|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/62555/eric-mika |website=Proballers |access-date=Feb 13, 2023 |date=Feb 13, 2023}}</ref>

===JL Bourg (2021–2022)===
On July 1, 2021, Mika signed with [[JL Bourg Basket|JL Bourg]] of [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jl-bourg-sign-eric-mika-rasheed-sulaimon/|title=JL Bourg sign Eric Mika, Rasheed Sulaimon|last=|first=|date=July 1, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 2, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===NBA G League Ignite (2022–2023)===
On September 28, 2022, Mika signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Roster Additions|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions/n-5885964|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 28, 2022|access-date=September 28, 2022}}</ref> and was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> On January 31, 2024, he was waived by the Ignite.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ignite Signs NBA G League Veteran Gabe York|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-signs-nba-g-league-veteran-gabe-york|website=NBA.com|date=January 31, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2024|archive-date=February 1, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240201030705/https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-signs-nba-g-league-veteran-gabe-york|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal==
Mika served as a [[Missionary (LDS Church)|missionary]] for [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] for two years in [[Rome, Italy]] between his freshman and sophomore years of college.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865596950/Eric-Mika-TJ-Haws-receive-mission-calls.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221013507/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865596950/Eric-Mika-TJ-Haws-receive-mission-calls.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 21, 2014 |title=Current, future BYU basketball players heading out on missions |first=Jeff |last=Call |work=DeseretNews.com |date=February 22, 2014 |accessdate=December 8, 2014}}</ref>
